newsitem.title: USA: Coastal ships Russian prod to U.S. through Estonia.
newsitem.headline: Coastal ships Russian prod to U.S. through Estonia.

text.p: Coastal Corp said it shipped its first tanker of Russian product to the U.S. from its new Tallinn Terminal in Estonia.

British Petroleum purchased the 45,624 metric tons (300,000 barrels) of straight-run M-100 fuel oil, which is set to arrive in New York on November 28. The fuel oil can be used as refinery feedstock or as fuel for ocean-going vessels.

Talk of Russian product rippled through U.S. cash markets in recent days. Jet fuel traders said low sulphur diesel prices firmed due to demand for the fuel to upgrade Russian gasoil into higher-quality heating oil for U.S. consumption.

The Coastal cargo was refined in Russia from Russian crude oil and shipped by rail to Coastal's terminal in Estonia. From there, it was transported through the Coastal Estonian joint venture's 4.6-mile pipeline to the Port of Muuga on the Baltic.

"The fact that our chartered tanker was the largest petroleum products ship ever loaded in Muuga Port shows the potential of our new facilities and import and export operations," said Coastal's chief executive officer David Arledge said in a prepared statement.
Tallinn Terminal is owned and operated by Estonia Oil Services Ltd (EOS) to market crude and products primarily from the former Soviet Union to Europe, North and South America and the Caribbean.
EOS Ltd is an Estonian subsidiary of Coastal Baltica Holding Company Ltd, which is jointly owned by a Coastal subsidiary and Baltica Finance NV, a Swedish-Dutch-owned company.
